verses.text: But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. Those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, on them the light has shined.
You have multiplied the nation. You have increased their joy.  They rejoice before you according to the joy in harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the plunder.
For the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, you have broken as in the day of Midian.
For all the armor of the armed man in the noisy battle, and the garments rolled in blood, will be for burning, fuel for the fire.
For to us a child is born. To us a son is given; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on David’s throne, and on his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from that time on, even forever. The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.
The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it falls on Israel.
All the people will know, including Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, who say in pride and in arrogance of heart,
“The bricks have fallen, but we will build with cut stone. The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place.”
Therefore Yahweh will set up on high against him the adversaries of Rezin, and will stir up his enemies,
The Syrians in front, and the Philistines behind; and they will devour Israel with open mouth. For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
Yet the people have not turned to him who struck them, neither have they sought Yahweh of Armies.
Therefore Yahweh will cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in one day.
The elder and the honorable man is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
For those who lead this people lead them astray; and those who are led by them are destroyed.

Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, neither will he have compassion on their fatherless and widows; for everyone is profane and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
For wickedness burns like a fire. It devours the briers and thorns; yes, it kindles in the thickets of the forest, and they roll upward in a column of smoke.
Through Yahweh of Armies’ wrath, the land is burned up; and the people are the fuel for the fire. No one spares his brother.
One will devour on the right hand, and be hungry; and he will eat on the left hand, and they will not be satisfied. Everyone will eat the flesh of his own arm:
Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh; and they together shall be against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

footnotes.content: Zebulun and Naphtali—northern lands laid low by war—will see glory again. The promise isn't that suffering disappears, but that the One who sees us in our anguish will transform that very place into a beacon. That's the nature of God's comfort: He doesn't ignore darkness, He walks through it and turns it to light.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Notice: *light*, not just the absence of darkness. A real shift. Those living in shadow of death—captives, the desperate, the forgotten—they see it first. The Gospel always reaches the most trapped heart first, and moves outward from there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The nation grows, joy multiplies—not through conquest or effort, but as a gift poured out. The joy *in harvest*, the joy of *dividing the spoils*—these are the deepest contentments a people know. Isaiah is painting a time when God's favor overflows so completely that even the quietest form of gladness seems inadequate.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Midian—that ancient victory when Gideon and three hundred defeated a vast army through God's power, not numbers. The yoke, the staff, the rod—all the instruments of oppression—broken the same way: not by strength, but by the Lord's hand alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the noise, blood, and machinery of war—the very armor men trusted in—will be fuel for the fire. A soldier's pride, his equipment, his wounds: all end in ash. Only in peace, never through more battle, does mankind find true rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: *To us a child is born.* The whole history of Israel—all the longing—narrows to this: a birth. And the names—Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace—they reveal Him. Not a human king with flaws, but one whose very nature brings healing and justice. This is Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His government—*endless* in its reach and time. Built on David's throne, upheld forever by *justice and righteousness*. Not the kingdoms we see rise and crumble, but one rooted in the character of God Himself. The zeal of Yahweh performs it—not our hands, but His burning heart for His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A word sent. Simple, decisive. The Lord speaks to Jacob—the whole family of God—and it falls on Israel like a stone cast into still water. Words from His mouth do what He intends; they don't return empty. Judgment is coming, but even judgment is His word, His attention.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ephraim and Samaria—the Northern Kingdom—they will *know* what the Lord is doing. But knowing and humbling oneself are different things. They speak in pride and arrogance, deaf to the very word falling on them. How often we receive a rebuke and hear only the sound of our own certainty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bricks fallen, sycamores cut—destruction in their land. Their answer: we'll rebuild with *finer* stone, plant *better* trees. Not a prayer, not a turning, just defiance dressed as ambition. How often do we meet hardship not with confession, but with a plan to show God how well we can manage without Him?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rezin was the king of Syria who allied against Judah. Now Yahweh says He will set up Rezin's enemies *against* Israel. In their pride they've invited judgment. The very powers they thought to manipulate become the rod in God's hand to discipline His stubborn people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Syrians in front, Philistines behind—squeezed between enemies. And the refrain: *his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.* It's like watching a beloved parent's patience run out, but not their care. The judgment continues not from indifference, but because He loves too much to stop.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The blow falls, but they don't turn. Their enemy strikes them, yet they don't seek Yahweh. I think of a child who, after being corrected, refuses to meet the parent's eyes, refuses the reconciliation being offered. How long does the Lord's hand stay stretched out in such refusal?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Head and tail, palm and reed—these are the whole people, from the greatest to the least. And in *one day*, the Lord will cut them off. It's the completeness of judgment: not just leaders, not just the common folk, but the entire structure of unfaithful society dismantled at once.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The head is the honored one, the prophet a deceiver—but the prophet *is* the tail, the seducer. Authority and false teaching together lead the people to ruin. Who do we follow in our own age? Whose voice—proud or humble, true or soothing—do we believe?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The leaders lead astray; those who follow are destroyed. It's not just the error of leadership, but the blindness of a people who cling to false shepherds. And the shame is shared: those who lead and those who follow are both complicit in their own downfall.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord will not rejoice over their young men—no comfort, no mercy. Everyone profane, everyone an evildoer, every mouth speaks folly. The judgment is thorough because the corruption is thorough. And still: *his hand is stretched out still*. Even in wrath, He offers the chance to turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wickedness is fire—it burns, consumes, spreads. The briers and thorns, the thickets—all devoured. There's an image of how sin multiplies: it doesn't stay confined, it rolls upward in smoke, choking out clean air, reaching others. Corruption is never solitary; it spreads like flame.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land burned by Yahweh's wrath; the people become fuel for the fire. No one spares his brother—even family bonds dissolve in the chaos. When God's judgment falls and a people have abandoned mercy, there's nothing left to hold them together. The social bonds tear like paper.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One devours on the right, hungers; eats on the left, unsatisfied. Even the act of consuming turns to cannibalism—eating their own arm. There's a visceral despair here: the insatiable hunger of a people turned on themselves, finding no rest, no satisfaction, only more emptiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Manasseh against Ephraim, Ephraim against Manasseh—brothers arrayed against brothers. Once united, now fractured. Readers today hear an echo in any age when a people divides against itself: when kinship breaks into faction, when neighbors become enemies. Only the Lord can mend what pride has torn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
